coverage_note: 00:26-06:10 is English small talk about the new app (no Arabic from Medi). Medi's Arabic is Latin-lettered until ~36:48, then mostly Arabic script. Amal's own lines are garbled by the engine in places (08:57/08:59 'سعود' for صوّروا, 10:14 'وحم', 43:07/43:29 'سيفاء' for عاصفة, 36:44 'زد أن دنع'). Left out as S4 pronunciation: 'ams' for حمّس (10:17), 'bansabit' for بنبسط (11:16, 54:52), 'joan' for جوعان (53:24), 'iħna biniz'aj' -> her 'ej sound' remark (33:44-33:54), 'Azajit' for أزعجت (51:40), 'إيه' for هي (57:49, 59:13), the 'Full، مش hot' remark on شبعان (55:23), and the ع-stress remarks at 50:50-51:28. Left out as self-fixes before she helped: 'inti maz'ooj' -> maz'ooja (25:12-25:27), 'biyaz'aju' -> biyaz'aj (33:21), 'baz'aj' -> 'bnz'aj' for مضارع of انزعج (44:28), 'بل أروح' -> 'قبل ما أروح' (39:53), 'أتعبك' -> 'أتعبها' (58:22, she had only prompted 'Her.' for the English), 'باتعب' -> 'أتعب' after لما (59:18). 'لما I make retired' (57:49) is English mid-sentence but he then produced the Arabic himself, so not filed as tier 3. 17:54 'futtuli in besit' is a meta question she did not follow (كيف؟). 19:17 'ma anbisit?' for 'don't enjoy' was accepted by her as ما انبسطت, so not filed. No swapped speaker labels noticed; Meet-chat lines are not marked in this transcript (21:42 she says she typed بزعج, the chat line itself is absent).

rows.medi_said: Did you enjoy, past tense, your time outside? Okay, so isn't it en-enbistee? Did you enjoy?
rows.amal_said: "انبسطتي." ... You forgot the double T and the "في."
rows.why: 2nd-person feminine past of انبسط needs the doubled t (انبسطتي); he said enbistee and she told him at 07:35-07:41 'it is double T ... you forgot the double T'.
rows.english: Did you (f) enjoy your time outside?

rows.medi_said: I think I gotta take that off. Enbas... Oh, I put enbustee. I put enbustee.
rows.amal_said: what is it-- what is missing? It's not "انبسطتي." Something is missing. What is it? ... "في"
rows.why: انبسط takes its fixed preposition في/بـ before the thing enjoyed; his written and spoken sentence had none, she asked what is missing and supplied في at 06:54.
rows.english: Did you enjoy your time outside?

rows.medi_said: Have fun, plural, and take many pictures. So enbistoo oo saweroo
rows.amal_said: "سعود. سعود." (engine garble of her cut-in; he then re-said Sawroo)
rows.why: Plural command of صوّر is صوّروا; he said saweroo, she cut in (her line is unreadable in the transcript) and he re-said Sawroo, then she said Great; low because her recast cannot be read and he may have self-fixed.
rows.english: Have fun and take many pictures.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, enbasat, didn't I?
rows.amal_said: You put "انبسط". ... does the تخيل have emotions? Does it get happy?
rows.why: Camping MADE everyone happy needs the causative بسط, not the get-happy انبسط; she asked whether camping has emotions and he switched to 'el takheem basat' at 10:10.
rows.english: Camping made everyone happy and excited.

rows.medi_said: el takheem basat kul hadha oo ams.
rows.amal_said: حم. بسط وحمس. ... Let's put the verbs together.
rows.why: He split the two verbs around the object (made everyone ... and excited); she recast the two verbs together 'بسط وحمس' and said 'let's put the verbs together', with the object after; 'ams' for حمّس is a dropped ح (S4, not counted).
rows.english: Camping made everyone happy and excited.

rows.medi_said: nafs?
rows.amal_said: الكل.
rows.why: She asked 'what's everyone?', he offered nafs (self/same), she gave الكل (sheet: all / everyone | Elkul | الكل); low because she then accepted his 'kul hadha' (كل حدا) as well at 10:55.

rows.medi_said: Is it, isn't it lisa ma bansabit?
rows.amal_said: This is I don't get happy yet. What about don't get happy? It's a command. ... ما تنبسط لسه.
rows.why: 'Don't get happy yet' is a negative command (ما + you-form تنبسط); he gave the b-present 'ma bansabit' (I don't get happy), she named it a command and gave ما تنبسط لسه at 11:52 after his 'ma teenbesit' at 11:47.

rows.medi_said: Yeah. Ma teenbesit lisa ma ba'arif kul shey.
rows.amal_said: Ma, we don't know.
rows.why: The target was 'we don't know everything'; he said the I-form ba'arif, she prompted 'we don't know' and he fixed to 'ma ben a'arif' at 12:01.
rows.english: Don't get happy yet, we don't know everything.

rows.medi_said: And if you say, like some- something is bisbat, bis- bibsit, that means it's fun.
rows.amal_said: بتبسط.
rows.why: He groped for the 3rd-person present of بسط ('it is fun' = it makes happy); she recast بتبسط; low because bisbat may be a sound slip (S4) rather than a wrong form, and she later (17:12) taught بتبسط/بيبسط as the adjective-like use.

rows.medi_said: Is that the same? Andesit ishish?
rows.amal_said: انبسطت؟ ... إي.
rows.why: 'Enjoy something' needs انبسط + بـ/في; he put the object straight after the verb, she echoed the bare verb as a prompt and he added 'be' at 14:24, which she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: Imbare lele or lele imbare
rows.amal_said: ليلة امبارح.
rows.why: She asked how to say 'last night' (15:31) and he did not have it ('Uh-oh', 'That's a new word we need to add'); she built it with him from ليلة + امبارح; his first order 'Imbare lele' is the idafa backwards (A2) but he hedged both orders and she picked the right one.

rows.medi_said: and anbisit, anbisit hafla- haflatik.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. We forgot something. ... في
rows.why: Same fixed preposition again: انبسط في; he dropped it, she said 'we forgot something' and he supplied fi at 18:51, she confirmed في at 18:57.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So ma'tanbisti halak.
rows.amal_said: I'm gonna keep making you repeat until you say في on your own. ... ما تنبسط بحالك. ... That's في or ب.
rows.why: Third miss of the preposition after انبسط in one drill; she said she will keep making him repeat until he says في on his own, he fixed to 'fi halak' at 20:02 and she gave ما تنبسط بحالك.

rows.medi_said: Fi halak. And I don't know how to say too much, right? ... Ziyadi?
rows.amal_said: You can say كتير. كتير or extra. كيف-- How do I say extra? ... زيادة.
rows.why: He said he did not know 'too much' and she supplied كتير; his guess Ziyadi/Ziyada she accepted as 'extra' (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة), so this is a didn't-know, not a wrong word.

rows.medi_said: so anbisti fi laylak.
rows.amal_said: This your night. One night. ... بليلتك. Yes. ليلتك.
rows.why: Feminine ليلة grows a -t- before the possessive ending (ليلتك) and Amal takes the -ik ending; he stuck -ak straight on layl, she prompted 'your night, one night', he fixed to laylatik at 20:49 and she confirmed ليلتك.

rows.medi_said: so I, I think I remembered mazuj as annoying and moza- mozaj as annoyed.
rows.amal_said: بالعكس. ... If it has this oo sound. مزعوج، موجوع، محروج، مجروح. All of them is annoyed. Feeling the thing, not causing it.
rows.why: He had the two adjectives swapped; she said بالعكس (the opposite) and gave the oo-pattern rule; sheet: annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج and annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج.

rows.medi_said: Mutab? ... No.
rows.amal_said: Do you remember متعب؟ ... is tiring. ... Same pattern as مزعج.
rows.why: She asked whether he remembers متعب, he said No, she supplied the meaning 'tiring' (same pattern as مزعج); a didn't-know, not a wrong word.

rows.medi_said: These voices or sounds are annoying. "hadhol el swat."
rows.amal_said: الأصوات.
rows.why: Plural of صوت is the broken plural أصوات; he said 'swat' without the initial a-, she recast الأصوات; low because it may be a dropped vowel (S4) rather than a wrong plural shape.

rows.medi_said: "Feeya za'ajat-za'ajatek."
rows.amal_said: أزعجتك. See? It's easier to say أزعجتك.
rows.why: She had asked for the a-form (أزعج, 'with an a') she introduced at 28:13; he produced bare زعجتك, she recast أزعجتك and he fixed to az'ajet; low because she said both forms exist and asked him to learn both.

rows.medi_said: You guys annoy him. Why is that my favorite? Az'aj, az'ajtu.
rows.amal_said: أزعجتُ. You can't say أزعجتُ، wo. Doesn't sound right. ... Yes, there is an h.
rows.why: 'You (pl) annoyed him' is أزعجتوا + the -h object ending (أزعجتوه); he stopped at az'ajtu, she said you can't say that and confirmed at 31:26 that the -h is there.

rows.medi_said: don't want to annoy them. Ana ma, ma bitti, az'ajkum.
rows.amal_said: أزعجهم.
rows.why: 'them' is the -hum ending (أزعجهم); he used -kum (you pl); she recast أزعجهم.
rows.english: I don't want to annoy them.

rows.medi_said: So, hadha al-jaw, annoys me. Baz- baz'ajni. Ana biyaz... biz'ajni.
rows.amal_said: almost. صح. بيزعجني.
rows.why: Subject is الجو (he/it) so the verb is بيزعجني; he started with the I-form prefix baz'aj- and only half-fixed to biz'ajni; she said 'almost' and recast بيزعجني twice.

rows.medi_said: So, don't annoy me. Ma ta'az-- Ma ta-- Ma ta'az'ajni. Ma ta'az'aj.
rows.amal_said: Which goes first؟ الـ ز أو الـ ع؟ ... ما تزعجني. ... ما تزعجيني.
rows.why: Negative command to Amal (f) is ما تزعجيني; he had the root letters in the wrong order (ta'az'aj) and the masc ending; she prompted which letter comes first, accepted ما تزعجني, then recast the feminine ما تزعجيني at 36:35; low because the letter order is a sound slip (S4).

rows.medi_said: So الولاد أزعجووو، أزعجووو،
rows.amal_said: أزعجوه؟
rows.why: 'The kids annoyed him' needs the -h object ending on أزعجوا (أزعجوه); he stretched the -u and never added the h, she recast أزعجوه and he repeated أزعجو at 37:25 still without it.

rows.medi_said: هو بيزعج، بيزعجوني.
rows.amal_said: بيزعج، ... بيزعجني.
rows.why: Subject هو takes بيزعج + ني; he inserted the plural -u- (بيزعجوني = they annoy me); she recast بيزعجني and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: Okay, so بي-بيزعج-بيزعجوني.
rows.amal_said: بزعجني.
rows.why: Same slip a minute later for 'it annoys me'; she recast بزعجني and he asked himself 'Why do I have the o in there?' before fixing to بيزعجني.

rows.medi_said: انزعجتم. انزعج، انزعجنا.
rows.why: 2nd-plural past in her Levantine ends in -tu (انزعجتوا, cf. her أزعجتوه drill at 31:26); -tum is MSA; she let it pass with طيب at 41:57.

rows.medi_said: Well, God. أنا نسيت الكلمة. أنا نسيت الكلمة.
rows.amal_said: سيفاء. (engine's rendering of عاصفة; he then said عاصفة، عاصفة)
rows.why: He said he forgot the word for storm and she supplied it (sheet: storm | 3aasefe | عاصفة); he then used it in انزعجنا من العاصفة at 43:18.

rows.medi_said: إنت بتنزعج. إنتي بتنزعجي. إنتو بتنزعجو. هي-- هو بينزعج. هي بتنزعج. هما بينزعجو. إحنا بنن-بننزعج.
rows.amal_said: Been catching you saying the instead of the ب. ... ننزعج.
rows.why: She says she has been catching him saying another consonant (transcribed 'the', most likely m-/n-) instead of the ب of the we-prefix (her form is bn-); the engine wrote his line with the ب so the slip is visible only in her remark.

rows.medi_said: ليش، ليش فرق من-- ليش فرق من WhatsApp?
rows.why: فرق is the noun 'difference'; 'why is it different' wants the adjective مختلف (sheet: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف) or ليش في فرق; she said كيف؟, he repeated it, and she just answered the meaning.
rows.english: Why is it different from WhatsApp?

rows.medi_said: ما تزع-- ما تزعجي. ما تزع-- ما، ما تن-- Oh yeah, that's right. ما تنزعج. ما تنزعج.
rows.amal_said: تنزعجي. ... ما تنزعجي. Cuz it's ززز، all of them together.
rows.why: 'Don't get annoyed' is the N-form انزعج (ما تنزعجي); he dropped to ما تزعجي (don't annoy); she recast تنزعجي at 48:13 and again ما تنزعجي at 48:33.

rows.medi_said: It does have an N. ma-matan, matanzajini.
rows.amal_said: No. ... By me. ما تنزعجي. ... Yes. ما تنزعجي مني.
rows.why: 'Annoyed BY me' is انزعج + من (مني), not the object ending -ni; she said No, prompted 'by me', and he produced matanzaji minni at 49:44; he had also first claimed it is 'without the N' at 48:47 and she asked ليش؟.

rows.medi_said: Matanzajini. I think I just need to slow it down. Matanzajini.
rows.amal_said: Yes. ما تزعجني. ما تنزعج مني. احكيهم التنتين. ... Yes. ما تزعجيني.
rows.why: Asked for 'don't annoy me' he kept producing the N-form (matanzajini = don't get annoyed + me) at 50:10, 50:47, 50:55, 51:13; she recast ما تزعجني / ما تزعجيني each time but framed it as stress on the ع, so this may be S4 rather than the get/make confusion.

rows.medi_said: So ana... Ana, so I get annoyed. It's present tense. Anabazaj. Na ba-banj.
rows.amal_said: Gets.
rows.why: 'I get annoyed' is the N-form بنزعج (sheet: i get annoyed | Ana banze3ej); he said bazaj (I annoy), she prompted 'Gets.' and he fixed to anabanzaj at 53:16.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I'm hungry.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, anabanzaj, lama...
rows.amal_said: If.
rows.why: The sentence is 'if I'm hungry'; he started لما (when), she prompted 'If.' and he fixed to Iza; sheet: if | Iza | إذا vs when (conditional) | Lamma | لما.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I'm hungry.

rows.medi_said: Oh, if. Iza. Iza akoon joan.
rows.amal_said: بس إذا بكون، مش أكون. ليش؟ ... If is conditional، but it doesn't take out the be. It keeps it.
rows.why: After إذا she wants the b-form بكون, not bare أكون; she stated the rule ('it doesn't take out the be') and he fixed to 'iza bakoon' at 54:03 and 54:10.

rows.medi_said: So I annoy who annoys me. أنا بزعج مين
rows.amal_said: mean or what's the better one؟ The one who. يلي.
rows.why: 'The one who annoys me' needs the relative اللي, not the question word مين; she asked for the better one and gave يلي, he said اللي at 56:19.
rows.english: I annoy the one who annoys me.

rows.medi_said: اللي who annoys me. Okay. So، اه، بينزعجني.
rows.amal_said: ليش أن annoys me.
rows.why: 'Annoys me' is the causative بيزعجني; he used the N-form بينزعجني (gets annoyed); she asked 'why the N, annoys me' and he fixed to بيزعجني at 56:47.

rows.medi_said: annoyed. أنا انزعجت.
rows.amal_said: I didn't get.
rows.why: He wanted 'I wasn't annoyed' but said the positive انزعجت; she prompted 'I didn't get' and he added ما at 1:00:55.

rows.medi_said: اه، أنا، اه، زعلان.
rows.amal_said: زعلت. Here's your internal flip. ... زعلت. ... أنا ما انزعجت، أنا زعلت.
rows.why: He paired the past verb ما انزعجت with the adjective زعلان; she recast the past verb زعلت ('I got sad') to match and called it his internal flip; the adjective alone would need كنت (B6).
rows.english: I wasn't annoyed, I was sad.

rows.medi_said: تعال. bye.
rows.why: تعال means 'come' (sheet: come | Ta3aal | تعال) and was said as a goodbye after her سلام; may be an engine mishearing of يلا.

rows.medi_said: shu ra7ty.
rows.amal_said: شو تحكي؟
rows.why: He seems to ask 'what did you say?' after her fast Arabic instruction, but ra7ty is 'you went'; she replied شو تحكي؟ (what are you saying?) and repeated the task in English, no explicit fix.

rows.medi_said: هو منزعج بي... نز-نزعج؟ Or is it انزعج؟
rows.amal_said: Just like we did in إنزع. Yes. Just like we did with انبسط.
rows.why: Asked for the past of بنزعج he first offered the participle منزعج and the bare نزعج before asking whether it is انزعج; she confirmed by pointing to انبسط and he said هو انزعج at 41:12; low because he reached it himself with only a confirmation.
